title: The UI thread
cards/0/body: As in WPF and Unity, Avalonia controls can be touched only from the UI thread. From any other thread you get InvalidOperationException: Call from invalid thread.
cards/1/q: A background thread writes to TextBlock.Text. What happens?
cards/1/options/2: The text updates after a delay
cards/1/explain: Controls check which thread is accessing them.
cards/3/title: Most of the time you do not need Dispatcher
cards/3/body: In an async command, await brings you back to the UI thread on its own: Avalonia installs its own SynchronizationContext. Hand heavy computation to Task.Run and assign the result after await.
cards/4/q: A command computes for 3 seconds right on the UI thread, and the window freezes. How do you fix it?
cards/4/options/0: Move the computation to Task.Run and await it
cards/4/explain: Post also runs the computation on the UI thread, so the window still freezes.
cards/5/q: Update the status from a background thread
cards/5/explain: Post queues the action on the UI thread.
cards/6/explain: System.Timers.Timer calls its handler on the thread pool. You need Dispatcher.UIThread.Post or a DispatcherTimer.
cards/7/q: Match each API to what it does
cards/7/pairs/0/1: Queue on the UI thread, do not wait
cards/7/pairs/1/1: Queue on the UI thread and wait
cards/7/pairs/2/1: Are we on the UI thread already?
cards/7/pairs/3/1: A timer that ticks on the UI thread
cards/8/q: What is true? Select all that apply.
cards/8/options/0: After await in a command, the code continues on the UI thread
cards/8/options/1: Task.Run moves heavy work off the UI thread
cards/8/options/2: .Result on the UI thread can hang the app
cards/8/options/3: Controls can be touched from any thread
cards/8/explain: The .Result deadlock is covered in detail in the "Async/await in depth" course.
